title: Choking, CPR, and Defibrillator (AED) Guide
summary: Immediate life-saving actions for adult and infant choking, chest compressions, and AED operation.
content:
1. Adult Choking:
- Encourage coughing if the person can breathe or speak.
- If coughing fails or airway is blocked: Lean the person forward. Give up to 5 sharp back blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand.
- If still blocked: Stand behind them, place a fist above their navel, grasp with your other hand, and pull sharply inwards and upwards (5 abdominal thrusts).
- Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts. Call 999 immediately if obstruction does not clear.

2. Infant Choking (Under 1 Year):
- Lay infant face-down along your forearm with head lower than chest.
- Give up to 5 gentle back blows with the heel of your hand.
- Turn infant face-up. Give up to 5 chest thrusts using two fingers on the centre of the chest. Never perform abdominal thrusts on infants.

3. Adult CPR:
- If unresponsive and not breathing normally, call 999 and request a defibrillator.
- Place the heel of your hand in the centre of the chest, interlock your other hand on top, and lock elbows.
- Compress the chest 5 to 6 cm deep at a rate of 100-120 beats per minute (to the rhythm of 'Stayin' Alive').
- Give 30 compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths. If untrained in rescue breaths, deliver continuous hands-only CPR compressions without stopping.

4. Public Access Defibrillator (AED):
- Open or turn on the AED. Voice prompts will guide you.
- Pull peel-off pads and stick them to bare, dry skin exactly as pictured on the pads.
- Stop CPR and do not touch the patient while the machine analyses heart rhythm.
- Press the flashing shock button only if instructed by the machine. Resume CPR immediately after shock.
